properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by the agent on 2026-10-07, from Anthony's words the same day: "a design pushes requirements/decisions to the lowest project level and that becomes the 'single source of truth' for the whole project". That principle is accepted intent (req:a-skill-run-in-a-session-holding-several-designs-writes-where-the-fact-belongs, from his 2026-09-22 "any fact only appears 'once'... should be at the lowest level").

THE TENSION: slice 3, ruled the same morning (dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs, "Once accepted"), plans that a requirement sent down arrives in the part as a COPY with its origin, accepted there by the part's owner. That copy was the agent's recommendation, to keep the part's design readable on its own (dec:nested-graphs). Anthony chose the binding (on acceptance) and the transport (write-only-at-proposed), and the copy came with that recommendation. A copy leaves two homes, the parent's and the part's, which the one-home principle says not to do.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) COPY WITH ORIGIN, as planned. Both designs read alone, and the origin watch reports when the parent's version moves. Two homes, kept honest by a check.
(b) MOVE. When the whole requirement belongs to one part, it leaves the parent and lives only in the part. The parent keeps a reference (the part's design id plus the node id) and reads its status from there. One home. The parent's design can no longer be read alone for that requirement, and a reference can dangle.
(c) DECOMPOSE. When a parent requirement spans parts, it stays in the parent as the whole's need, and each part holds its OWN smaller requirement DECOMPOSES-linked across designs (the cross-design relation of dec:idea-a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-so-linking-works-on-the-one-design). No text is duplicated; each piece has one home.
(d) (b) when a requirement is wholly one part's, (c) when it spans several, and a copy never. Probably the honest systems-engineering answer: allocation is either whole or decomposed, and a copy is neither.

COST: (a) is what slice 3 plans. (b) and (c) need a typed cross-design reference, the same one the relation idea needs. That one piece serves all three ideas, so (d) costs little more than (a) once the reference exists.

COUNTERPOINTS:
- Under (b) a parent's view of its own requirements depends on reaching every part. At work that may mean a server the parent's reader cannot reach, so the parent sees a reference it cannot open.
- A copy is what every other engineering tool does (a requirement flowed down into a subsystem specification). People recognise it.
- Decisions differ: a decision governs locally once accepted, so a local node, a copy, may be needed for GOVERNED_BY to point at.



═══ SETTLED 2026-10-07 — OPTION (d): MOVE OR DECOMPOSE, NEVER COPY ═══
Anthony, 2026-10-07, asked for the agent's recommendation on the four open choices and replied "Go with your picks". The pick:
- REQUIREMENTS: one that belongs wholly to one part MOVES; the part becomes its single home, and the parent keeps a cross-design link and reads its status from the part. One that spans parts DECOMPOSES; the parent keeps the whole's need, and each part holds its own piece, linked DECOMPOSES across designs to the parent's.
- DECISIONS: a decision stays in the parent. What a part must do BECAUSE of it lands in the part as DERIVED requirements (or constraints), linked to the parent's decision. The why is reachable by link and never duplicated, so a part never holds a second copy of a decision it did not make.
- Binding is unchanged (dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs, 'Once accepted'): what lands in the part is proposed until the part's owner accepts it.
Why over copying: the 09-22 single-source rule applied consistently; allocation is either whole or decomposed, and a copy is neither; a moved item has nothing to drift. Cost accepted: it depends on the cross-design link, and a parent's reader who cannot reach a part sees a link, not the text.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-07 — a requirement sent down MOVES to the part when it is wholly the part's, DECOMPOSES when it spans parts, and is never copied; a decision stays in the parent and flows down as derived requirements
properties.rationale: Recorded so that the slice 3 plan is built knowingly against the one-home principle, or changed, before any code exists. It is cheaper to settle now than after received copies are in people's designs.
